chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The first thing Allah the Almighty will judge regarding on the Day of Resurrection is the blood [deeds of murderers], so He will make the two sons of Adam stand [for judgment] and judge between them. Then those who follow them from the companions of blood [victims and murderers], until none of them remain. Then the people after that. The slain will come to his killer, and his blood will splash in his face, and he will say: 'This one killed me.' He will say: 'You killed him.' And he will not be able to hide anything from Allah.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ الدِّمَاءِ: Companions of blood (those involved in killing)
key_terms.ابْنَیْ آدَمَ: The two sons of Adam (Habil and Qabil, representing the first murder)

ai.seo_question: What is the first matter Allah judges on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq narrates that the Day of Resurrection begins with the adjudication of 'blood' (al-Dima'), prioritizing the retribution of the slain over all other matters. This tradition emphasizes the physical manifestation of justice, where the victim's blood literally 'sprinkles' on the killer's face as an undeniable witness, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the tangible reality of divine recompense for homicide.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from al-Muffadhal b. Salih from Jabir b. Yazid from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“The Almighty Allah will account for the deeds of the murderers first on the Day of Judgment. He will gather all murderers and the victims. Every victim will stand near his/her murderer with a bleeding face. He will tell Allah: This person had murdered me. Allah will ask the murderer: Did you murder him? And the person will not be able to hide anything from Him.”
